title.title: Every minimal class VII surface with $b_2 > 0$ has a shell
title.subtitle: Claim: every minimal class VII surface with $b_2 > 0$ contains a global spherical shell

plain: The last unclassified kind of complex surface turns out to be a Hopf surface with some points blown up

object.caption: second Betti number $b_2$ of a minimal class VII surface

beats.text: Class VII surfaces: the last unclassified piece of the Kodaira classification
Teleman proved $b_2 = 1$ (2005) and $b_2 = 2$ (2010) with gauge theory
The claim covers every $b_2 > 0$ in one uniform argument

achievement.label: Nakamura's global spherical shell conjecture
achievement.context: Before: $b_2 = 1$ and $b_2 = 2$ by Teleman; general $b_2$ open
achievement.note: If it holds, minimal class VII surfaces with $b_2 > 0$ are classified

verify.detail: No Lean; a uniform 39-page proof where Teleman needed case-specific work
verify.ourCheck: We read the claim and caveats; we did not check the proof

voice.text: Class seven surfaces are the last unclassified compact complex surfaces.
A spherical shell in each would make it a blown-up Hopf surface.
Claimed: each one with b two positive has a shell.

sources.quote: b2 = 1 by Teleman (Invent. Math. 2005), b2 = 2 by Teleman (Annals 2010)

sources.ref: article, The global spherical shell conjecture (family 060)
sources.quote: The paper claims all $b_2>0$ in 39 pages
